messages:
Maya (SE): Hey team, spinning up a POC for Acme Corp. They're hitting structured output failures when we use function-calling + json_mode. Also getting intermittent 429s. Can someone help triage?
Ethan (AE): customer blocked on this for demo tomorrow — asking about any recommended config and whether retries will blow up pricing.
Maya (SE): Error from logs: `JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)` after function call returns. Sometimes model returns `\"result\": { ... }` double-escaped, sometimes plain JSON.
Riley (Eng): hmm are you using streaming? we've seen stream framing break JSON mode if chunks split braces.
Maya (SE): they're calling with `json_mode: true` and `stream: true` (default).
Riley (Eng): try disabling stream for the POC or enable `json_mode: \"relaxed\"` if available — streaming + strict JSON can yield partial frames. Also set `max_output_tokens` so model doesn't truncate mid-object.
Maya (SE): good call. Any quick snippet I can send?
Riley (Eng): send this: ```json\n{\"call\": {\"name\": \"extract_entities\"}, \"json_mode\": \"relaxed\", \"max_output_tokens\": 512}\n```
Ethan (AE): noted. What about the 429s? customer sees `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` then `retry-after: 15` in headers.
Devon (SRE): looks like they're on bursty test traffic. For Hosted tiers we recommend client-side exponential backoff with jitter — start at 500ms, cap at 10s. Also consider request batching on your side.
Maya (SE): customer worried backoff = higher cost. Is there a pricing/backoff guidance we can give?
Ethan (AE): they asked if we bill for retries — yes each request counts against usage. Provide tips: reduce token usage, use caching for repeated prompts, use dedicated for predictable throughput.
Nora (Security): one more thing: Acme's security team will need the dataflow diagram and assurance they're not hitting our shared tenancy logs. We need to escalate Private deployment options.
Maya (SE): can you add a note about logs retention and KMS?
Nora (Security): Short answer: hosted logs are retained 30 days by default, we offer KMS integrations on Dedicated/Private. Will prepare an SQA blurb.
Ethan (AE): customer also wants a way to validate schema before accepting function output — any quick client-side safety checks?
Riley (Eng): yes — run a lightweight JSON schema validator on the client before calling downstream services. Example: `ajv.validate(schema, payload)` and reject if invalid. Also we add an envelope check: verify payload starts with `{` and ends with `}` when not streaming.
Maya (SE): they saw some outputs like `OK:\n{\"result\": ...}` — how to strip prefixes safely?
Riley (Eng): heuristic: find first `{` and last `}` and parse substring, but beware of braces in strings. Better to ask model to output only the JSON object (system prompt) and add `stop` tokens immediately after object.
Ethan (AE): customer asking for an ETA on Dedicated review to avoid 429s in demo — can we fast-track?
Devon (SRE): I can open a capacity exception for a short window if AE provides expected QPS and time window. Need channel, date, start/end, and max RPS.
Maya (SE): I'll collect numbers. One last gotcha: their tooling automatically escapes JSON when embedding in another JSON field which caused double-escaping. Any mitigation?
Riley (Eng): avoid double serialization — send function arguments as native objects if SDK supports it. If you're POSTing JSON stringified again, you'll get escapes. Example: don't do `JSON.stringify({arg: JSON.stringify(obj)})`.
Maya (SE): thanks. I'll send the snippet, retry guidance, and security note to the customer.
Ethan (AE): if you can cc me on the capacity request that'd be great.
ops-bot: Deploy request created (#DC-4321) — tag @Devon.
Devon (SRE): saw the ticket. I'll review and reply with a short-term bump if quota allows.
Maya (SE): awesome — will follow up after applying the relaxed json_mode + disable streaming and report back. :thumbsup:
Ethan (AE): thanks all, big help.
Maya (SE): closing loop: fixed by disabling stream + client-side JSON sanitizer. Demo passed. Customer asked for written runbook — I'll draft and share in #sales-docs.
